summary:
The plan is a double cross: a north–south body crossed by three east–west bars, with two big planted courtyards and smaller courts between them. The wings are 12-storey flat-roofed blocks in beige smooth sandstone, with a grid of 3-block bays of recessed dark windows and about 1 in 6 lit. Every wing ends in a blank 13-storey squared tower, as in the photo.
In the middle, a stepped-up central block carries a floodlit penthouse and masts with red aircraft lights, and every roof is a lit slab deck behind a quartz coping line. The west front on Shifu Road has a quartz-columned canopy, the name, the city emblem and flagpoles, and the camera-facing south and east fronts get the most lit windows and floodlit tower panels. Double-cross civic block: 12-storey sandstone wings with piered dark-window grid, 13-storey blank towers, stepped central block with floodlit quartz crown and red-lit masts. West Shifu Rd portico with lit glass hall, emblem, flagpoles; planted courts with fountains.
Facades, roofs and lights are split by trade so S/E faces and roofs read at dusk.

Massing and shell: parts/shell.mjs lays a polished_andesite plinth (y0..1) under every mass and a hollow black_concrete core wall 4 cells in from each exposed face, computed from a union heightmap, so wings, towers, central block and podia merge. The face depths 0..3 stay empty for facades; openings and courts are untouched. make.sh is clean and `mcd check` reports no floating blocks. I did not look at the render tiles.
polish: The plinth is y0..1, not y0..2: y2 is left for the ground-storey piers and lintels. The facade part must place its own face skin, glass and backing at depths 0..3.
The spurs M1/M15 got only a y0 plinth, so spurPavilion must supply their walls and floor at y1.
No roof decks or parapets: the roof part owns y62, 67, 15 and 10. The core wall tops out at deck-1, one block under the deck.
I did not tick the elements.md items. The shell only provides the massing and backing for the wall skin and tower items.
The plinth helper uses replace:true, which overwrites the ground dirt and grass under the footprints at y0..1.

waste.what: Wrote a distance-transform wall-offset routine to get a clean inner wall across overlapping masses of different heights
waste.cost: about 60 lines of code and 2 fix iterations (tier gaps, floating wall)
waste.tool: a build-library helper such as unionShell(g, boxes, {depth, block, top}) that builds a hollow inner wall for a union of boxes with per-box heights

companions.task: Run the floating-block and enclosed-cell check after each tier change

summary:
Roofs and terraces: parts/roofs.mjs builds every flat deck at top-2 (wings 62, towers and M7 67, podia 15, spurs 10), with parapets on exposed edges only, coping caps and inner-ring lanterns every 8.
Also places the 3 penthouses, the 9 tower plant boxes, 4 podium planters, the M7c crown walls and slab roof (y68..74), and a y1 spur floor. make.sh saves a whole build.nbt: roof part placed 42743 blocks, 0 refused, 0 off-palette.
Checked: aerial render of the roof reads as decks, parapets, crown and terraces. Spur decks still float until facades build spurPavilion's pillars and glass.
polish: Spur decks (M1, M15) float in `mcd check` until the facade part's spurPavilion pillars and glass are built, because the spine's only ground is the y1 floor I added.
The coping is flush on the parapet top, not 1 proud as the plan's cornice line says. I did not add an overhanging cornice because it would float outside the wall.
The crown band (P6) must use crownBand(..., { over: true }) because the crown walls are smooth_quartz from my part.
The lamp posts on the podia (elements item Podia, the lampPost part) are not built here.
I did not use roof.json or the roof tool. The plan asks for hand-built flat decks, so `runParts` skipped the roof spec, and the trusses/gable steps do not apply.

waste.what: Copied the shell's mass list (M, SPURS) into roofs.mjs, because shell.mjs does not export it. Every later part will need the same list.
waste.cost: about 30 lines duplicated, one place to drift
waste.tool: Export MASSES and SPURS from a shared plan module (for example vocab/masses.mjs) so the shell, roofs and facades read one source.

waste.what: Worked out tower and podium centres (plant-box cx/cz, planter boxes) by hand from the plan's x/z ranges.
waste.cost: 9 plant-box centres and 4 planter boxes computed by hand, with rounding checks
waste.tool: A helper like towerCentres() or a mass lookup by id (plan.md Masses table as data), so plantBox and planter take a mass id.

waste.what: Wrote my own owner-grid deck loop because roofDeck() takes one box. Taller neighbours must take the shared edge, so the box helper cannot be used on the stepped massing.
waste.cost: about 60 lines of custom loop, two retries (a neighbour-index bounds bug and the spur sky/door cells)
waste.tool: roofDeck accepting an owner grid (or a per-cell top function) and an exposed-edge rule: a parapet only where the neighbour is open or lower.

waste.what: Checked the roof by hand against the spur skylight and door cells (x84..86 at z0 and z374). The check tool reported the lantern under the skylight, and I fixed it after the fact.
waste.cost: one rebuild and one structure check
waste.tool: mcd check with the spur skylight and door cells as named openings, or a reserve list passed to runParts

companions.task: The cornice: a 1-proud smooth_quartz coping that overhangs the parapet on a corbel or bracket, and the flat-deck drainage slope (no water pooling at the spurs).
The spur skylight glass at y10 and the pavilion's glass panes, which hold the spur deck up until the facade part builds its pillars.
The podium planting and the courtyard trees (oak_log and jungle_log trunks, persistent leaves), so the terraces read as planted rather than as bare moss blocks.
The roof lantern spacing and the dusk light levels on every deck, checked with mcd light so no roof cell is dark enough for a mob to spawn.

summary:
Facades: Facades built in parts/facades.mjs: office bay grid with exposure test on all wings, central block and podia; ground-storey glazing; tower slot faces with joints and quoins; lit windows; court, podium, east and spur-end lit entries; spur pavilions with skylight.
make.sh produces a whole build.nbt with no REFUSED writes and no OFF-PALETTE blocks from the facade part. The front-left and right-elevation renders show the office grids reading on the wings.
Not done: T5/T8/T9 white_terracotta panels, the floodlight course (P6), podium third-storey bays, and the slab ramp at z374 (portico's). Tower slot lanterns have no backing, and some white_terracotta spandrels read as orphans at wing ends.
polish: T5, T8 and T9 white_terracotta panels (the tower face is blank smooth sandstone with slots only), and the ochre_froglight floodlight course at y 62 on the T4/T5/T7 east and T8/T9 south faces (plan item P6).
Podium M2 and M14 have only the 7-storey bay row; the third storey (y 12..16) is filled plain smooth sandstone, with no bays, because the roof parapet at y 16 would collide.
Lit tower slots are sea_lantern at depth 1 with no black_concrete backing, so the checker flags them as unsupported; towerFace would need a backing for lit slots.
Some white_terracotta spandrels at wing ends show as orphans in the structure check (for example at 81,11,35 and 104,61,36).

M8 west centre (x 18, z 170..207, y <= 12) is left clear for the portico's lobby glass and doors; the shroomlight behind the emblem at (18,30,188) sits in my bay cell, so the portico part may be refused there.
The slab ramp at z 374 is not mine (portico/grounds). I did not run mcd fit or the walk check, and the roof, which the roofs part provides, is absent from my renders.

waste.what: Worked out wing face geometry by hand: which bays are exposed, outward neighbour tops, and the along/inward/depth-to-xz mapping for every face.
waste.cost: about 15 minutes of reasoning and two rewrites
waste.tool: A face-frame helper in the build library (face -> at(along, depth, y), with exposure against the mass table) and an exposed-face query over the massing, so facade parts stop re-deriving the same mapping.

waste.what: Patched around spurPavilion writing the bare id "glass" (not in the palette) with a proxy grid view, after first trying a g.set wrapper that recursed.
waste.cost: 3 rebuilds
waste.tool: Fix the vocab's skylight id to gray_stained_glass (or a palette-checked helper), so no wrapper is needed.

waste.what: Chose and hand-wrote the door and entry openings (court doors, podium, east, spur ends) from plan OPENINGS coordinates.
waste.cost: about 10 coordinate sets
waste.tool: An openings table in base.mjs read by the facade and shell parts, so each opening is defined once and every part skips it the same way.

waste.what: Checked the face by eye from elevation renders only; the structure check's orphan and unsupported lists were read by hand.
waste.cost: 2 renders, 1 check
waste.tool: mcd fit on the facade cells, plus a per-face coverage report (which wall cells are filled, opened or open air).

companions.task: Fit the lit lobby and entry glass, the spur skylight and the spur end doors, with the connected panes set along the walls.
Dress the tower faces and quoins with the cut_sandstone joints and the white_terracotta panels, and take the podium third-storey walls up to the parapet.
Hang the court and entry doors (iron doors and their thresholds) and the spur end doors, with the entrance approach checked.
Lay the lit-window pattern and its backing, so the dusk lighting reads evenly across the facades.

summary:
Portico and west front: Portico and west front built in parts/portico.mjs: apron and portico floor at y1 (polished_andesite with light_gray joints), six quartz columns, smooth_quartz canopy at y13 with a y13..15 fascia and 36 sea_lanterns under it, and the glass hall at x19 with four iron doors at x18 (they replace the M8 grass at y2).
Also six flagpoles (x4/9/14 at z165 and z212) and four lamp posts. make.sh saves a whole build.nbt with 2710 placed, 0 refused, and no off-palette blocks except wall-banner variants; fit is OK.
Not done: the name letters placed 0 (no air cell in front of the x0 fascia), and the emblem disc floats until the facade skin at x18 exists.
polish: Name 'TAIPEI CITY HALL' not placed: nameBand/bannerWord writes only into air in front of the board, and the board is the x0 fascia with x -1 off the plot. Fix: move the board to x1 (canopy edge) or clear the fascia cells where the letters go, then re-run nameBand.

City emblem disc at x17 (y26..34, z184..192) is FLOATING in this isolated build: the M8 west face at x18 is the facades part's skin, which is not built here. Check it attaches after the merge; the shroomlight at (18,30,188) is written only into air and may be refused then.

Interpretation: the plan's ramp ('bottom slabs at y1.5, then the deck') conflicts with the column bases at x1 in cell y2. I laid the columns first, then bottom slabs at y2 on the x0 cells and the x1 cells between columns (surface 2.5 at the street edge, 2.0 apron). The threshold at x18 is level (2.0), so the way in has one half step at the street edge only.

M8 footing is grass at y2 (ground 2 from layGround), so the lobby floor inside x19..30 is grass. The glass hall and doors replace that grass only at their own cells. Someone needs to pave the lobby floor (smooth_stone, per plan FLOORS) if the lights or facades parts do not.
mcd check reports the 36 canopy sea_lanterns at y12 as UNSUPPORTED ('nothing below to hang from'). They are flush under the canopy at y13, so this looks like a checker false positive for sea_lantern.
White and red wall banners (flagpole banners, via B.banner) are reported off-palette because palette.json lists only standing banner ids. Same item family; kept.
Lamp posts are at x6 and x16 on z168 and z209 (apron, north and south), not the 'every 8' spacing; flagpole banners hang on the west side as the plan says.

waste.what: Worked out each portico cell and door/glass position by hand from the plan (column corners, canopy fascia, door leaves, paving joints), then verified each one by reading single cells with g.get.
waste.cost: about 15 spot-check reads and 4 rebuild-and-check cycles
waste.tool: a portico/entrance helper that takes the plan's named rows (columns, doors, fascia span) and reports which cells were refused or already occupied

waste.what: Wrote a local doubleDoorOver because vocab doubleDoor only takes air, and the M8 footing is grass at y2 that the door must replace.
waste.cost: one retry after the doors came out missing
waste.tool: a `doubleDoor(g, pos, facing, { over: ["grass_block"] })` option, or a ground-aware writer that treats ground-layer cells as replaceable for the part's own footprint

waste.what: Found by trial that nameBand and bannerWord write only into air, so a board on the x0 fascia gets 0 letters, and a letter board needs air in front of it.
waste.cost: one full make and a read of the placed cells
waste.tool: nameBand/bannerWord option to place letters on a named solid board (or to clear the board cells first), and a check that warns when a letter board has no free cell in front

waste.what: Read the ground and shell layout (which cells are grass at y1 and y2) by hand to decide the paving and ramp heights.
waste.cost: several node one-liners to read groundAt and cell blocks
waste.tool: a `mcd cells build.nbt --box x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1` table that prints the block per cell, plus a groundAt-aware summary

waste.what: Ran mcd check and fit separately, then grepped their output to see which lines mattered; the sea_lantern false positive had to be recognised by eye.
waste.cost: 3 check runs
waste.tool: a check filter (--only section,kind) or a per-part report that lists only the findings inside that part's box

companions.task: Lay out 'TAIPEI CITY HALL' in blue banner letters on a proper board in front of the west fascia (the x0 face has no air in front of it), so the name is placed and reads from Shifu Road.
Check the apron lamp posts and the canopy sea_lantern row for even light on the portico floor, and suggest the spacing that the plan's 'every 8' asks for.
Confirm the ramp and column bases: the half step at the street edge, and how the x1 column cells interrupt the slab run at y2.

summary:
Courtyards and grounds: Built parts/grounds.mjs: CN/CS courts with 4-wide cross paths, fountain basins, 10-grid trees and fountain lamps; CNE tree row, CNW paving and trees, CSE/CSW planters; west apron paving and lamp posts.
make.sh produces a whole build.nbt with this part: 5,462 blocks placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; mcd check is clean and mcd fit reports OK.
Courtyard interiors were checked by block-column probes and one apron zoom, not by an eye-level court render (the north court is walled in from the north view).
polish: Courtyard look not visually verified: the north-view zoom of CN was black (wings block the eye), so tree shapes and fountain read are unchecked; needs a dusk render from inside the court or the hero camera.

Court surface height: plan.md says courts are at y 2, but the GROUND map gives CN, CNE, CNW lawn at y 1 (north block) and CS and the south courts at y 2. I followed the map and logged it in plan.md Notes; the plan owner should confirm.
Fountain basin floors are not solid: CN water sits at y 0..1 on the dirt stack with nothing below, and the CS basin water sits at y 1..2 on dirt. A quartz floor would need a shell-level decision.
Ground patches (coarse_dirt, podzol, rooted_dirt) are not built: they are not in palette.json, so the lawn is plain grass with no patchy mix.
Lamp posts stand only at the fountain corners and on the apron. None line the cross paths, which the trade rule (every 8-10 blocks along a path) asks for; the lights part may add them.
Apron paving and lamp posts overlap the portico's P4 scope; I wrote them into the Notes so the portico part does not pave those cells again.
No walk test: mcd walk was not run on the court paths, and the path-to-door connection (CN x55 z84..85 door to the z84..87 path) was checked by reading the plan, not by walking it.

waste.what: Worked out the court grid by hand: tree positions on the 10-grid, skipping the path rows, columns and fountain cells, one court at a time; then fixed the fountain/path overlap by hand.
waste.cost: about 6 coordinate passes over CN, CS, CNE, CNW, CSE and CSW, plus 2 rewrites of the path loop
waste.tool: a courtLayout(court, {pathX, pathZ, basin, every: 10, offset: 5}) helper in vocab/h4 that returns tree, path and lamp cells, with the basin and path priority built in

waste.what: Paving over grass cells by hand, one g.set per column with a groundAt and grass check, because the vocab helpers refuse non-air.
waste.cost: about 1,500 per-column checks written as my own surface() loop
waste.tool: a surfaceFill(g, box, block, {onlyOver: 'grass_block', ground: true}) helper that follows the groundAt height and replaces only the layGround grass

waste.what: Checked the fountain, path, apron and tree columns by writing a probe script that loads build.nbt and reads block columns.
waste.cost: one probe script, roughly 8 lines, rerun after each change
waste.tool: mcd column build.nbt x,z (print the block column from y0 to y8) so the probe does not need to be written

waste.what: Checked the court surface height by reading the GROUND map cell by cell against plan.md's 'y 2' text.
waste.cost: about 4 minutes of reasoning
waste.tool: mcd ground <kit dir> --cell x,z, or a plan line that states each court's surface y from GROUND, so a conflict is caught at plan time

companions.task: Settle the court surface heights (y 1 or y 2) and the court paths, to confirm the plan against the GROUND map before any planting goes in.
Build the fountain basin floors and the quartz rim as solid work, so the basins hold water without relying on the dirt stack.
Choose the tree species and crown forms for the 10-grid courts (oak, jungle, a tall spruce for accents) and check the crown clearance over the doors and paths.
Light the cross paths with lamp posts every 8-10 blocks and check the court dark cells with mcd light on the court floors.

summary:
Dusk lighting and crown: Built parts/lights.mjs (3208 blocks, 0 refused, 0 off-palette): the M7c crown (smooth_quartz ring walls, full lid at y74, pearlescent band and ochre slot via crownBand, hung lanterns inside), an ochre light slot inset on M7 at y68, floodlight courses at y62 on the E faces (x197) and S faces (z332), four masts at y75..80 with a red redstone_torch, and lit M8 hall and spur-spine floors with hung lanterns.
Verified: make.sh saves a whole build.nbt; the front-right render shows the crown in place at the M7 centre. Build and check output are attributable to this part; floating and unsupported flags come only from the stub parts, not from lights.
polish: Floodlight courses (x197 E faces, z332 S faces at y62) are air-only: if the facades part fills those cells first they are refused at merge. Check the REFUSED line in make.sh after the merge.
The crown walls and the M7 light slot float in this copy because the roofs part has not laid the M7 deck at y67 yet; they should be supported after the merge.
The spur-spine hung lanterns at y9 need the spur deck at y10 (spurPavilion, roofs/facades). Fit flags them as hanging from air until that lands.
The M7 light slot sits at depth 1 behind the parapet, so it lights the roof from above and is not visible from the street. Moving it proud would need a roofs-part change.
The tower redstone_torch on each plant box (y71) comes from plantBox in the roofs part, not from lights.
Not verified: the lit-roofs-and-terraces claim, since the roofs part is still a stub here. No clock is in this part's spec, so no clock was built.

waste.what: Worked out the floodlight run coordinates (x197 and z332 spans per tower) and the crown and M7 inset rectangles by hand, then re-derived them after each edit.
waste.cost: about 6 coordinate lists, 2 reruns
waste.tool: a plan-to-coordinates helper that takes a plan.md table row (mass id, face, span) and returns the course box, or a named-span lookup in vocab/base.mjs (e.g. TOWER_FACES).

waste.what: mast() puts a standing redstone_torch directly on a lightning_rod, which Minecraft rejects, so I hand-wrote the mast column (bars, rod, quartz cap, torch).
waste.cost: one failed build check plus a rewrite of the mast loop (about 6 blocks)
waste.tool: fix vocab/h2.mjs mast() to end in a full-block cap before the torch, and say so in its comment.

waste.what: Chose between sea_lantern and hung lantern for the hall and spur ceilings by running check and reading UNSUPPORTED flags, one rebuild per try.
waste.cost: 2 full make and check cycles
waste.tool: a lamp-placement helper (ceilingLamps(box, y, step)) that picks lantern hanging=true under a solid block and states the support rule, so a lamp is never placed unsupported.

waste.what: Wrote a local crown-walls ring loop and an interior hung-lantern grid; each one repeats the put-if-air guard.
waste.cost: about 30 lines of loops
waste.tool: a shared vocab helper box shell (ring of a material over a box, air-only) so parts stop re-writing the same ring loops.

waste.what: Used a macOS sed -i one-liner that failed on the BSD suffix argument and skipped the build step.
waste.cost: one retry
waste.tool: use the Edit tool or node for in-place text changes in this environment.

companions.task: Lay the M7 deck at y67 under the crown and the spur deck at y10 so my crown walls and hung spur lanterns have support; lay the crown lid as their roof only if they want it, since I placed a full smooth_quartz lid at y74.
Leave the tower floodlight slots at y62 (x197, z332) and the M8 hall glass wall as air, so my lights land flush in the wall plane instead of being refused at merge.

summary:
inspection: Fixed the FIT problem: roof decks were bottom slabs, leaving half a block of air under the parapets and penthouses set on them. The deck, spur deck and crown roof slab are now top slabs (same smooth_stone / smooth_quartz blocks, same heights).
WALK is ok with no rooms listed, so nothing changed for it. make.sh rebuilt build.nbt; the walk check passes and the fit check reports OK with 0 issues (was 4117).
Edited parts/roofs.mjs (deck, crown roof) and vocab/h2.mjs (roofDeck, spurPavilion deck). Palette unchanged.
polish: vocab/h2.mjs roofDeck doc comment still says 'bottom slab' for the deck; the code now uses a top slab (comment only, no effect on the build).

waste.what: Worked out from source which helper made the floating blocks: the fit list named only 8 of 4117 cells, all parapet cells at deck+1 over a bottom-slab deck, so the root cause had to be traced into roofs.mjs and vocab/h2.mjs by hand.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls to grep and read roof code; 0 blocks placed by hand
waste.tool: mcd fit should group issues by cause (the block below and the helper or part that placed it, e.g. 'roof deck bottom slab at y62, placed by roofs.mjs') instead of listing 4117 cells one line each.

waste.what: Found the walk and fit targets by reasoning about which parts used the deck slab, rather than from the check output.
waste.cost: one grep across parts/ and vocab/
waste.tool: mcd fit --summary with a per-source count and the placing module would have located the fix at once.
